The minimal number of pieces is **611**.

**Setup.** Each student must receive $221/403$ of an apple in total. Since $221 = 13 \cdot 17$ and $403 = 13 \cdot 31$, the share is $17/31$.

**Lower bound.** Model the situation as a bipartite graph with 221 apple-vertices and 403 student-vertices. Each piece is an edge joining the apple it came from to the student who receives it. Group the vertices into connected components. A component containing $a_i$ apples and $b_i$ students must satisfy $a_i/b_i = 221/403 = 17/31$, so $a_i$ is a multiple of 17 and $b_i$ is a multiple of 31. A connected component on $a_i + b_i$ vertices needs at least $a_i + b_i - 1$ edges, so the total number of pieces is at least

$$\sum_i (a_i + b_i - 1) = 221 + 403 - (\text{number of components}).$$

Each component contains at least 17 apples, so there are at most $221/17 = 13$ components. Therefore the number of pieces is at least $221 + 403 - 13 = 611$.

**Construction.** Split the problem into 13 independent groups, each with 17 apples and 31 students. In each group, share the 17 apples among the 31 students, each student getting $17/31$. This can be done with $17 + 31 - 1 = 47$ pieces. For example, lay the 17 apples in a row and cut them so that the cut points are at multiples of $1/31$ along the total length of 17 apples; this gives 31 pieces of length $17/31$, and each student takes one. Counting the cuts gives $17 + 30 = 47$ pieces, and the groups together use $13 \cdot 47 = 611$ pieces.

This matches the general formula $a + b - \gcd(a,b) = 221 + 403 - 13 = 611$.

ANSWER: 611
